metadata.title: The role of parental involvement in adolescents’ digital reading performance

survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: The study uses PISA 2018 microdata with a hierarchical structure (students nested within schools, nested within countries) and explicitly normalizes the student weight W_FSTUWT to promote unbiased estimates. The analytic sample is restricted to countries that administered both the student and parent questionnaires, and the authors further exclude a subset of students (e.g., special education needs or language differences) before modeling. The models are estimated using a three-level HLM framework (country–school–student), which aligns with the complex sampling structure. The manuscript does not report replicate-weight procedures (e.g., BRR/jackknife), so uncertainty quantification is described through the HLM and Rubin’s rules for combining multiply imputed datasets rather than replicate-based variance estimation.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: The study uses PISA 2018 reading-themed cycle data for 15-year-old students and restricts to countries that voluntarily administered both the student questionnaire and the parent questionnaire (to ensure parental involvement measures could be linked to each student). Students are included at the 15-year-old age level, with exclusions for special education needs or language differences. Parent-questionnaire variables used in the study have <30% missingness except EXPECTAP_4, which is excluded from analysis; the remaining missingness is handled via multiple imputation. The authors also align each imputed dataset with the corresponding plausible value (MI1 with PV1, etc.) and then combine results using Rubin’s rules.

main_findings.performance_metrics: Three-level HLM (country–school–student) with PVREAD; fixed effects (Model 3): PRESUPP β=0.021 (SE=0.004, p<0.001), CURSUPP β=-0.041 (SE=0.003, p<0.001), PASCHPOL β=-0.047 (SE=0.003, p<0.001), EMOSUPP β=0.055 (SE=0.003, p<0.001), JOYREADP β=0.060 (SE=0.003, p<0.001). Interaction: PREEMO (PRECUPP×EMOSUPP) positive (reported as only significant positive interaction). Random effects: student f2=8.429%, school f2=49.630%, country f2=86.076%.
main_findings.standardized_conclusion: Using PISA 2018 Reading data (digital reading performance; PVREAD 1–10), the study leveraged previous parental support, current parental support, school policies for parental behavioral involvement, parental emotional support, and parental enjoyment of reading to model digital reading performance, finding that previous support was positively associated while current support and school policies were negatively associated. It also found that parental emotional support and parental enjoyment of reading were positively correlated with performance, and that the interaction between previous support and emotional support was the only significant positive interaction. This indicates that strengthening emotionally supportive and enjoyment-oriented parental involvement—while avoiding potentially counterproductive forms of current support or intrusive school-policy involvement—may be more effective for adolescents’ digital reading outcomes, though the study is correlational and cannot establish causal effects.

data.outcome_summary: The study analyzes PISA 2018 digital reading performance (10 plausible values, PVREAD 1–10) for 15-year-old students in 12 countries (total N=83,043; 3,342 schools), linking student and parent questionnaire data and adding the country-level ICT Development Index (IDI). It estimates a three-level HLM (country–school–student) and handles missing parent-questionnaire data via multiple imputation, matching each imputed dataset to the corresponding plausible value and combining results using Rubin’s rules. In the full model, previous parental support in reading-related activities is positively associated with digital reading performance (β=0.021, p<0.001), while current parental support and school policies for parental behavioral involvement are negatively associated (β=-0.041 and β=-0.047, both p<0.001). Parental emotional support (β=0.055) and parental enjoyment of reading (β=0.060) are positively correlated with performance (both p<0.001), and only the interaction between previous support and emotional support shows a positive effect. Because the design is cross-sectional and the analysis is correlational, these associations should not be interpreted as causal impacts of parental involvement.
data.null_fields_interpretation: This paper is an empirical correlational study using three-level HLM with multiple imputation and plausible-value combining, but it does not train or evaluate any machine-learning predictive models. As a result, the ML technique fields are intentionally left empty (no ML algorithms are reported), and the extraction focuses on the multilevel modeling results rather than predictive accuracy.
